payload.title: Add secure login to this application.

contract.goal: Implement passwordless email magic-link login endpoints (POST /auth/request, POST /auth/verify, POST /auth/logout, GET /me) reusing the existing UserRepo, SessionStore and EmailSender
constraints: Magic-link tokens expire after 15 minutes and are single-use; store only SHA-256 hashes
Session is an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie named session backed by SessionStore, 24h TTL
Unknown emails get the same 202 as known ones (no account enumeration)

DELEGATION EXPECTED: the token store (src/auth/token-store.ts with create/consume/expiry + tests/auth/token-store.test.ts) is a separable module. Delegate it as a subtask with relay_propose_subtask (recipient token-dev, runtime codex, allowed_paths src/auth/token-store.ts and tests/auth/token-store.test.ts, machine-checked criteria) and wait for it with relay_await_task before wiring the routes. Do not implement the token store yourself.

acceptance_criteria.condition: Requesting a link then verifying the token creates a session and GET /me returns the user
The whole test suite passes, including the delegated token store tests
Changes stay within the allowed scope

interpretation: Add a Hono sub-app in src/auth/routes.ts with POST /auth/request (body {email}; always 202 {status:'sent'} whether or not the email is known; for known users create a magic-link token via the delegated TokenStore and send it with the existing EmailSender), POST /auth/verify (body {token}; consumes the single-use token, creates a 24h session in SessionStore, sets the session cookie, returns 200 with the user), POST /auth/logout (revokes the cookie's session in SessionStore, clears the cookie, returns 204), and replace the placeholder GET /me in src/app.ts so it returns 200 with the user when a valid session cookie exists and keeps the existing 401 {error:'not authenticated'} otherwise.

src/auth/session-cookie.ts holds the cookie name 'session', the 24h TTL constant, and helpers to build the Set-Cookie header (HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; Max-Age) plus a clearing header and a cookie reader, so routes.ts and app.ts share one definition.

createApp in src/app.ts gains an optional dependencies object (users, sessions, email, tokens, clock) with the existing defaults, so existing callers (server.ts, tests/app.test.ts) keep working unchanged and tests/auth/routes.test.ts can inject MemoryEmailSender and a fake clock to prove expiry and single use.

The token store (src/auth/token-store.ts + tests/auth/token-store.test.ts) is delegated to token-dev via relay_propose_subtask with a fixed interface (create(subject) -> raw token, consume(rawToken) -> subject | undefined, SHA-256 hashes only, 15-minute default TTL, injectable clock) and awaited with relay_await_task before the routes are exercised; I will not implement it myself.

tests/auth/routes.test.ts covers the end-to-end request -> read token from the stub email -> verify -> GET /me flow, plus 202 for unknown emails, token single use, token expiry after 15 minutes, session expiry after 24h, cookie attributes, logout, and 400 on malformed bodies.
assumptions: Payloads are JSON: POST /auth/request expects {email: string}; POST /auth/verify expects {token: string}. Malformed bodies return 400 {error:'invalid request'}. An invalid, expired or already-used token returns 401 {error:'invalid or expired token'}. Logout without a valid session still returns 204 and clears the cookie (idempotent).

The raw token is delivered inside the stub email text as a link of the form <APP_BASE_URL or http://localhost:3000>/auth/verify?token=<raw>, and the token also appears on its own line so tests can extract it; no HTML email.
The magic-link token is bound to the user's id (subject) at request time; the token store never sees raw tokens after creation and stores only SHA-256 hashes, expiry, and subject.
The cookie is not marked Secure because the demo runs over plain http on localhost; adding Secure would break local cookies. This is documented in a comment in session-cookie.ts.
No token is created or email sent for unknown emails; the 202 response body and status are byte-identical to the known-email case.
risks: The routes cannot be run until the delegated token store lands; if the subtask fails or is canceled I will report a blocker rather than implement the store myself, since the contract forbids that.

The token-dev implementation must match the interface I specify in the subtask contract (module path, class name, method signatures); a mismatch would surface as a type error in routes.ts and require a repair round.
tests/app.test.ts is outside my scope and asserts the unauthenticated /me response; the implementation must preserve that exact 401 body.
Timing differences between known and unknown emails (token creation and email send) are a residual enumeration side channel that the contract does not ask me to close.

verification_plan.AC-1: Run `npx vitest run tests/auth/routes.test.ts` in the worktree and confirm the end-to-end test (POST /auth/request -> extract token from MemoryEmailSender.sent -> POST /auth/verify -> capture Set-Cookie -> GET /me with cookie returns 200 with the seeded user) passes together with the single-use, expiry, cookie-attribute, logout and 202-for-unknown-email tests.
verification_plan.AC-2: After the delegated token store subtask reports completed, merge or check out its branch state as instructed by relay_await_task, then run `npx vitest run` (all suites including tests/auth/token-store.test.ts and the pre-existing tests) and `npx tsc --noEmit`, confirming zero failures.
verification_plan.AC-3: Run `git status --porcelain` and `git diff --name-only <base>` in the worktree and confirm every changed path is one of src/auth/routes.ts, src/auth/session-cookie.ts, src/app.ts, tests/auth/routes.test.ts; the token store files belong to the subtask's disjoint scope and are not touched by me.

contract.goal: Implement a single-use, expiring magic-link token store in src/auth/token-store.ts that stores only SHA-256 hashes of tokens, with Vitest coverage in tests/auth/token-store.test.ts
constraints: Create src/auth/token-store.ts exporting exactly this public API (the parent task's routes are written against it, so names and signatures must match): `export const MAGIC_LINK_TTL_MS = 15 * 60 * 1000;` `export const hashToken = (rawToken: string): string` (hex SHA-256 via node:crypto createHash('sha256')); `export interface TokenStoreOptions { now?: () => number; ttlMs?: number }`; `export class TokenStore { constructor(options?: TokenStoreOptions); create(subject: string): string; consume(rawToken: string): string | undefined; }`.

create(subject) generates a cryptographically random token (node:crypto randomBytes(32) encoded as base64url or hex), stores ONLY { hash: hashToken(rawToken), subject, expiresAt: now() + ttlMs } keyed by the hash, and returns the raw token. The raw token must never be kept in memory by the store after create returns.

consume(rawToken) hashes the input, looks up the entry, deletes it, and returns its subject only if the entry exists and expiresAt >= now(). Expired or unknown entries return undefined; expired entries are deleted on lookup. A second consume of the same token returns undefined (single use).
Default ttlMs is MAGIC_LINK_TTL_MS (15 minutes); default now is Date.now. The constructor throws if ttlMs is not a finite positive number, mirroring SessionStore.
Follow the style of src/session/store.ts: ES module imports with .js extensions, strict TypeScript, no new dependencies, no console output.

tests/auth/token-store.test.ts must use an injected mutable clock and cover at least: create returns a non-empty token and consume returns the subject; consume of an unknown token returns undefined; a token cannot be consumed twice; a token consumed exactly at now = expiresAt still works and at now = expiresAt + 1 returns undefined; two create calls return different tokens; hashToken('abc') equals the known SHA-256 hex digest 'ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad'; the store does not retain the raw token (e.g. inspect via JSON.stringify(store) or Object.values of its private map and assert the raw token string does not appear).
non_goals: HTTP routes, cookies, sessions, email sending, user lookup, persistence beyond process memory
Editing any file outside src/auth/token-store.ts and tests/auth/token-store.test.ts

acceptance_criteria.condition: The token store tests pass and cover creation, single use, expiry boundary, unknown tokens, hashing, and non-retention of raw tokens
The module typechecks under the project's strict configuration together with the rest of the repository
The store hashes tokens with SHA-256 and exports the agreed public API names

payload.message: Contract accepted. Delegated token store to token-dev as subtask t-token-store (src/auth/token-store.ts + tests). Writing session-cookie helper, routes and routes tests against the agreed TokenStore interface while waiting.

interpretation: Implement the exact specified exports and an in-memory TokenStore in src/auth/token-store.ts.
Generate 32-byte cryptographically random raw tokens, retain only their SHA-256 hashes with subject and inclusive expiry, and delete entries on every matching consume.
Add focused Vitest coverage for success, unknown and repeated consumption, expiry boundaries, uniqueness, known hashing, and raw-token non-retention.
assumptions: Use base64url encoding for randomBytes(32); the contract explicitly permits base64url or hex.
Use a private Map keyed by the hash, consistent with an in-process store and the stated non-goal of persistence.
An entry is valid when expiresAt >= now(), as explicitly stated.
risks: Runtime/private-field serialization behavior could make a weak non-retention test; the test will inspect both serialization and the store's internal values at runtime.
Existing repository conventions may impose TypeScript details beyond the summary; implementation will mirror src/session/store.ts.

submission.summary: Passwordless magic-link login. POST /auth/request {email} always returns 202 {status:'sent'}; for known users it creates a TokenStore token (delegated to t-token-store, SHA-256 hashed, 15-min single-use) and sends a link <baseUrl>/auth/verify?token=... via EmailSender. POST /auth/verify {token} consumes the token, creates a 24h SessionStore session, sets an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax Path=/ 'session' cookie (Max-Age 86400, not Secure because the demo runs on http://localhost) and returns the user; invalid/expired/reused tokens get 401. POST /auth/logout revokes the session and clears the cookie (204, idempotent). GET /me returns the user for a valid session and keeps the original 401 {error:'not authenticated'} otherwise. createApp now takes an optional dependencies object (users, sessions, tokens, email, baseUrl) with the previous defaults, so server.ts and existing tests are unchanged. Subtask t-token-store was verified and fast-forwarded into this branch as commit 26e3cb5.
